page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 50 GB SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core capabilities. The server achieves top-tier status in stress-ng single-core CPU performance with a score of 3401.48 and single-threaded gzip compression at 38.71 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 14316.03 and PassMark CPU scoring 10193.28, both placing in the middle 50%. Memory performance presents a notable tradeoff; while cached small-block read bandwidth is average at 775.54 GB/sec, the PassMark memory score falls into the bottom 25% at 1329.77.

This server is configured for workloads requiring moderate, balanced resources. It handles static web serving at 10.62 GB/sec and Redis SET operations at 9.82 million operations per second. However, resource-intensive tasks like medium-model LLM prompt processing perform poorly, averaging 16.46 tokens per second. Given the shared CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance offers a cost-effective entry point for general-purpose applications, development environments, and lightweight database operations rather than sustained high-compute or memory-heavy tasks.
